root_cause: The offcanvas component unconditionally sets aria-modal='true' and role='dialog' when shown, making it behave as a modal even when the backdrop is disabled (data-bs-backdrop='false'). This traps focus inside the offcanvas via _enforceFocusOnElement, preventing tab navigation to the amount field within the allowed number of tab presses.
repair_strategy: Make the offcanvas respect the backdrop setting: only apply aria-modal and role='dialog' when backdrop is true. When backdrop is false, keep the offcanvas non-modal so focus can leave it naturally, allowing users to tab to the amount field. The hide method already safely removes these attributes unconditionally (removeAttribute is harmless if they were never set).
expected_accessibility_effect: Users can tab from the help trigger to the amount field in two tab presses when the non-modal help panel is open, satisfying WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order) and 2.1.1 (keyboard).
functional_risks: When backdrop is true, the offcanvas must remain modal; the conditional ensures attributes are still applied.
Removing the attributes when backdrop is false may change how assistive technologies announce the offcanvas, but this aligns with the intended non-modal behavior.
Ensure that the hide method continues to safely remove the attributes (removeAttribute is harmless if they were never set).
verification_requirements: With data-bs-backdrop='false', verify that focus reaches #amount within ≤2 tab presses after opening the offcanvas.
With data-bs-backdrop='true' (or default), verify that focus is trapped inside the offcanvas and cannot tab to #amount until it is closed.
Confirm that the offcanvas still opens, closes, and responds to the Close help button and Escape key as expected.
